adcp_version.description: Release-precision AdCP version (VERSION.RELEASE, e.g. "3.0", "3.1", "3.1-beta"). On a request: the buyer's release pin — the seller validates against its supported_versions and returns VERSION_UNSUPPORTED on cross-major mismatch, or downshifts to the highest supported release within the same major. On a response: the release the seller actually served — clients SHOULD validate the response against that release's schema, not against their pin. Patches are not negotiated; surface them as build_version on capabilities for operational visibility. When omitted, falls back to adcp_major_version (deprecated) or server default. Buyers SHOULD emit both adcp_version and adcp_major_version through 3.x to remain compatible with sellers that only read the legacy field. NORMALIZATION: SDKs that read full-semver values from bundle metadata (e.g. ComplianceIndex.published_version = "3.1.0-beta.1") MUST normalize to release-precision ("3.1-beta.1") before emitting on the wire — meta-field values are NOT valid wire values.

adcp_major_version.description: DEPRECATED in favor of adcp_version (release-precision string). Servers MUST continue to honor this field through 3.x. Removed in 4.0. Original semantics: the AdCP major version the buyer's payloads conform to. Sellers validate against their supported major_versions and return VERSION_UNSUPPORTED if unsupported. When omitted, the seller assumes its highest supported version.

action.description: report is seller-authenticated and creates a non-authoritative record; review is plan-owner-authenticated and accepts or disputes it.

outcome_id.description: Completed outcome whose authoritative commitment is being adjusted.

adjustment_id.description: Adjustment to accept or dispute. Required for review.

decision.description: Buyer review decision. Acceptance is blocked while delivery evidence for the governed action is disputed in an open governance period; a historical closed_unresolved period is audit evidence, not a billing determination.

seller_reference.description: Seller resource identifier. Must exactly match the reference retained on the source outcome.

seller_adjustment_id.description: Stable identifier of the adjustment in the authenticated seller's system.

adjustment_type.description: Commercial meaning. Verified decommitments restore headroom in every mode; verified refunds and credits restore it only in verified_net_cost mode; makegoods never restore cash headroom.

amount.description: Positive adjustment amount in the plan currency.

reason.description: Human-readable reason retained in the audit trail.

effective_at.description: When the seller's adjustment became effective.

evidence.description: Integrity-bound commercial source record supplied by the seller. Its evidence_type must correspond to adjustment_type.

description: Two-party append-only adjustment lifecycle. The authenticated seller reports commercial evidence; the authenticated plan owner later accepts or disputes that exact record. Reporting alone never changes net cost or headroom.
